text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's National Assembly has passed the country's new constitution. The charter needs to be approved by the president and the nationwide referendum.

- Poland will not be a strategic economic partner for Russia as it is troubled with its own economic problems and has neither the economic nor technologocal potential to participate in reforming the Russian economy, the head of Russia's Economic Reform Centre, Sergei Pawlenko, said.

- The opposition Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) should tighten links with the centrist Union for Freedom party (UW) to avoid being a replica of the populist Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP), the former Foreign Minister Andrzej Olechowski said. AWS should not limit its political appeal to frustrated anti-communists, said Aleksander Hall, a leader of the Conservative Peasants' Party (SKL), which belongs to AWS.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The Elektrownia Belchatow power plant will construct a new 800 MW power bloc at a cost of $1 billion. About $200 million will come from a joint venture to be set up to finance the project and the remainder from banking loans and an Eurobond issue. The new block will be operational in 2003, the plant's management said.

- Around 70 companies from Poland and neighbouring countries exhibited their products last week at the Spring '97 construction, carpentry and interior decoration fair in Bialystok, northeastern Poland.

- Progress, Victoria and Piast are the most successful National Investment Funds (NFI) of Poland's mass privatisation scheme regarding industrial sector concentration, development strategy and transparency, a report by Merrill Lynch dated March 17 said.
- Around 49 percent of Poles have no savings at all, whereas 34 percent save money in banks or through other financial instruments, a recent survey by the PBS polling institute said.
NOWA EUROPA
- British Airways (BA) has opened a branch office in Krakow, southern Poland. The airline will start a Krakow-London connection in the end of this months, BA said.

- Poland's advertising market grew by 34 percent last year, compared with 1995, a report by the BR TVP SA state-owned television broadcasters' advertising and marketing research department said. The corporate sector spent $700 million on advertising campaigns last year.
- The Atlantis construction material producer will issue five million shares worth up to seven zlotys per share in April this year, the company said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Around 2.5 million households have subscribed to cable televison in the past few years, a report by the Polish Cable TV Association said. Polska Televizja Kablowa (PTK) cable TV newwork is planning to take over the Gosat company while Aster City will merge with the Porion cable television. By the end of the decade the market will be dominated by several big firms.
ZYCIE

- Japan's new Toyota car plant is more likely to be set up in Poland rather than France, The Economist weekly said. No practical gains will result from locating a new plant in France, Toyota's president Hiroshi Okuda said.
- Poland's air carrier LOT and Italy's Alitalia will jointly operate the daily Warsaw-Rome and Warsaw-Milan flights, the airlines said.
